cues.en: Which different types of components do we have?
And now, please, let me note that these are not official differentiations, not official types.
You don't create these different components differently.
You don't have to annotate them or set a specific specific configuration.
Instead, it's just about how you use them in any app you're building and actually with any framework,
be that a compiler like Svelte or be that a real framework like Angular or Vue or a library like React,
you typically have stateful components, also called containers and presentational components.
Now what's the difference?
Stateful components are all about holding and managing data and passing data around to other components.
The state in stateful is basically the data, and stateful means that this data is not necessarily static,
but that it may change, may change because of user interaction, because it's fetched from a server
for whatever reason.
In a presentational component you might have some static data, but besides that, all the data you
you use in that component is received from outside and in a presentational component, you typically
also don't change that data, you don't manipulate it, instead you just output it.
You might also output a button that allows the user to interact, but then you would always just take
that interaction and pass it back to a stateful component so that the stateful component can act and
change data or whatever needs to be done.
Examples for stateful components in general could be your app component, which often is a root place
for data management or main feature components.
If you're building a shop that could be products or checkout components in our app, we might later
have some meet ups component that helps us with managing meet ups.
Presentational component examples would be things like modals cards, buttons, So basically user interface
elements you could say, or also something like our meet up item in this app, we're building components
that simply output something and shouldn't really change our data.
Now why do we have this differentiation?
Why doesn't every component do what it needs to do and change data if it has a button and instead of
passing that action back to another component which then changes data?
The idea here is that we keep our app maintainable.
If every component does everything, it's pretty hard to manage your application as it grows, especially
if you're working in a team.
Instead, if you have a few sources of truth, as it's also called, so only a few components which
are changing stuff, then the vast majority of components is pretty easy to manage and you don't really
need to worry about whether that component edits or changes your meet up data.
You know, I only got two components which interact with meet up data.
All the other components are only there so that I can encapsulate my styles and my markup and output
content in a nice and pleasant way.
So this differentiation is something you see in any framework and it makes a lot of sense because it
ensures that your app stays maintainable and therefore you only have a few stateful components typically,
and you have plenty of presentational components.
